framework: ISO/IEC TR 24027:2021 Information technology - Artificial intelligence (AI) - Bias in AI systems and AI aided decision making
requirement_paraphrase: The catalogue page says the report describes measurement techniques and methods for assessing bias, with all AI system lifecycle phases in scope, including testing, evaluation and use.
what_is_tested: Bias in AI systems and AI aided decision making
interpretation_note: Read only the Standards Council of Canada catalogue entry, not the report. A technical report is informative; no clause level claim is made.

framework: IEEE 2802-2022 IEEE Standard for Performance and Safety Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence Based Medical Devices: Terminology
requirement_paraphrase: The catalogue description says the standard establishes concepts and terminology for performance and safety evaluation of AI based medical devices, covering technology, datasets, quality characteristics and quality evaluation, with an annex of basic equations for quality evaluation.
what_is_tested: Performance and safety of AI based medical devices (terminology only)
interpretation_note: Terminology standard; it defines vocabulary rather than requiring a test. Page lists it as an active standard, published 2023-05-05. Abstract level only.

framework: IEEE 2937-2022 IEEE Standard for Performance Benchmarking for Artificial Intelligence Server Systems
requirement_paraphrase: The catalogue description says the standard gives formal methods for benchmarking the performance of AI server systems, including approaches for test, metrics and measurement, and discusses technical requirements for benchmarking tools.
what_is_tested: Performance of AI server systems, clusters and high performance computing infrastructure
interpretation_note: Infrastructure benchmarking, not testing of model behaviour. Page lists it as an active standard, published 2022-09-14. Abstract level only.

framework: IEEE 3129-2023 IEEE Standard for Robustness Testing and Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based Image Recognition Service
requirement_paraphrase: The catalogue description says the standard provides test specifications and indicators for common corruption and adversarial attacks, describes robustness attack threats, and sets out an assessment framework to evaluate robustness of image recognition services under varied settings.
what_is_tested: Robustness of AI based image recognition services against common corruption and adversarial attacks
interpretation_note: Abstract level only; the test specifications themselves were not read. Page lists it as an active standard, published 2023-06-02.

framework: ITU-T F.748.44 Assessment criteria for foundation models - Benchmark
requirement_paraphrase: The catalogue summary says the Recommendation covers requirements and evaluation methods of foundation models and gives an overview of benchmarking, aiming at consistency, transparency and comparability.
what_is_tested: Foundation models (benchmark requirements and evaluation methods)
interpretation_note: ITU-T Recommendations are not binding unless adopted by a member. The page gives no detail of the requirements; page shows status in force, approved 2025-03-16. Abstract level only.

framework: ETSI EN 304 223 V2.1.1 Securing Artificial Intelligence (SAI); Baseline Cyber Security Requirements for AI Models and Systems
requirement_paraphrase: Released models must have been tested as part of a security assessment process, and System Operators are to conduct testing before the system is deployed, with support from Developers.
what_is_tested: Security of AI models and systems before release and deployment
interpretation_note: Marked shall in the summary I received. European Standard of a technical committee; no regulatory mandate was seen in the passages read, so coded voluntary. Wording and page numbers came through a summariser and should be checked against the PDF.

framework: ETSI EN 304 223 V2.1.1 Securing Artificial Intelligence (SAI); Baseline Cyber Security Requirements for AI Models and Systems
requirement_paraphrase: Recommended: use independent security testers with technical skills relevant to the AI system; share testing findings with System Operators; and evaluate model outputs so that they do not let operators or end users reverse engineer the model or gain unintended influence over the system.
what_is_tested: Security assessment findings and model outputs
who_tests: Independent security testers; Developers; System Operators
interpretation_note: Marked should in the summary received. Summary-level reading; the tool reported that red teaming is not named in this principle. Locators as reported by the summariser.

framework: ETSI EN 304 223 V2.1.1 Securing Artificial Intelligence (SAI); Baseline Cyber Security Requirements for AI Models and Systems
requirement_paraphrase: Recommended: treat a major update as a new model version and undertake a new security testing and evaluation process for it.
what_is_tested: Security of updated models
interpretation_note: Marked should in the summary received; it works as a retest trigger after major updates. Summary-level reading.

framework: ETSI TS 104 275 V1.1.1 Securing Artificial Intelligence (SAI); Application of Baseline Cyber Security Requirements principles to Generative AI; Preventing Harm from Deepfakes
requirement_paraphrase: Principle 9 adds no provision extensions and defers to EN 304 223; a note says the testing and evaluation could take the form of red team testing and/or adversarial testing, for example prompt testing in multiple languages.
what_is_tested: Generative AI systems, with deepfake harm as the use case
who_tests: locator not seen for the actor; defers to EN 304 223
interpretation_note: The red team wording is a note with 'could', so informative only. Summary-level reading.

framework: ETSI TS 104 275 V1.1.1 Securing Artificial Intelligence (SAI); Application of Baseline Cyber Security Requirements principles to Generative AI; Preventing Harm from Deepfakes
requirement_paraphrase: Annex C gives conformance test cases, each with a test purpose, method and pass or fail verdict, for several principle clauses (for example C.2.3.2 pre-deployment risk assessment, p. 22-23). The summary reported no test case for Principle 9.
what_is_tested: Conformance with the principles' provisions, including pre-deployment risk assessment
interpretation_note: The lister's note that Annex C covers Principle 9 was not borne out in the summary I received: no Principle 9 test case was reported. Summary-level reading.

framework: Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence (OECD/LEGAL/0449), adopted 22 May 2019, amended 8 Nov 2023 and 3 May 2024 as read
clause_or_page: Section I, definition of AI system lifecycle
requirement_paraphrase: The lifecycle definition lists test, evaluate, verify and validate as one of its phases, and says phases are often iterative rather than strictly sequential.
what_is_tested: AI system across its lifecycle
interpretation_note: The Recommendation is a non binding OECD instrument; the principles are addressed to adherents and AI actors. Summary-level reading.

framework: Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence (OECD/LEGAL/0449), adopted 22 May 2019, amended 8 Nov 2023 and 3 May 2024 as read
requirement_paraphrase: AI systems should be robust, secure and safe throughout their lifecycle, functioning appropriately under normal use, foreseeable use or misuse, or adverse conditions.
what_is_tested: Robustness, security and safety of AI systems
interpretation_note: Does not name a test; testing is only implied. 'Should' in a non binding recommendation. Summary-level reading.

framework: Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence (OECD/LEGAL/0449), adopted 22 May 2019, amended 8 Nov 2023 and 3 May 2024 as read
requirement_paraphrase: Governments should consider using experimentation to provide a controlled environment in which AI systems can be tested, and scaled up as appropriate.
what_is_tested: AI systems in controlled experimentation environments
interpretation_note: Describes policy for regulatory sandboxes, not a duty on developers. Summary-level reading.

framework: Hiroshima Process International Code of Conduct for Organizations Developing Advanced AI Systems (G7; date not stated in the text received)
requirement_paraphrase: Organizations should use diverse internal and independent external testing measures, including adversarial testing, and apply suitable mitigations for identified risks; testing should occur in secure environments and at several checkpoints, in particular before deployment and market placement.
what_is_tested: Advanced AI systems across risks, using red teaming and other measures
who_tests: Developing organisations, with independent external testers
interpretation_note: The Code is voluntary guidance for organisations; wording as reported by the summariser, with quoted phrases under 15 words. Pages as reported.

framework: Hiroshima Process International Code of Conduct for Organizations Developing Advanced AI Systems (G7; date not stated in the text received)
requirement_paraphrase: Organizations should publicly report capabilities, limitations and domains of appropriate and inappropriate use, and publish transparency reports for significant new releases, covering evaluation results including red teaming results.
what_is_tested: Reporting of evaluation results
interpretation_note: Reporting step that follows testing; coded enabler. Summary-level reading.

framework: Hiroshima Process International Code of Conduct for Organizations Developing Advanced AI Systems (G7; date not stated in the text received)
requirement_paraphrase: Organizations should monitor for vulnerabilities, incidents, emerging risks and misuse after deployment and act on what they find.
what_is_tested: Deployed advanced AI systems
interpretation_note: Post deployment monitoring rather than testing as such. Summary-level reading.

framework: The Bletchley Declaration by Countries Attending the AI Safety Summit, 1-2 November 2023 (gov.uk policy paper, page last updated 13 February 2025)
clause_or_page: Declaration body, paragraph beginning 'We affirm that, whilst safety must be considered across the AI lifecycle' (paragraph position as reported by the fetch summary)
requirement_paraphrase: Actors developing frontier AI capabilities carry a particularly strong responsibility for safety, to be met through measures including safety testing by way of evaluations (wording seen: 'systems for safety testing, through evaluations').
what_is_tested: Safety of frontier AI systems, by evaluation
interpretation_note: A political declaration by attending countries, not a legal instrument; it states a responsibility but sets no test method, threshold or enforcement. Locator comes from a summary, so paragraph counting should be checked against the page.

framework: The Bletchley Declaration by Countries Attending the AI Safety Summit, 1-2 November 2023 (gov.uk policy paper, page last updated 13 February 2025)
clause_or_page: Agenda for frontier AI risk, second bullet (position as reported by the fetch summary)
requirement_paraphrase: Countries' cooperation agenda includes risk based national policies and developer transparency, with a focus on suitable evaluation metrics and tools for safety testing (wording seen: 'appropriate evaluation metrics, tools for safety testing').
what_is_tested: Evaluation metrics and safety testing tools (to be developed)
who_tests: Signatory governments and private frontier developers (cooperation)
interpretation_note: Describes a shared research and policy agenda rather than a testing duty on any actor. Coded enabler because it concerns the means of testing. Primary type OTHER because no specific test category is named.

framework: International AI Safety Report, Second Key Update: Technical Safeguards and Risk Management (25 November 2025)
clause_or_page: Section 1 Introduction, para. 2 (no page numbers in text read)
requirement_paraphrase: Reports that three leading developers applied enhanced safeguards to new models because their internal pre deployment testing could not rule out possible help with biological weapons misuse (wording seen: 'could not rule out').
what_is_tested: Biological misuse uplift (dangerous capability), internal pre deployment testing
interpretation_note: A scientific report, not normative; it describes practice reported in developer system cards and sets no requirement. Coded context.

framework: International AI Safety Report, Second Key Update: Technical Safeguards and Risk Management (25 November 2025)
clause_or_page: Section 2 Technical methods, 'Sophisticated attackers routinely find ways...' (no page numbers in text read)
requirement_paraphrase: Describes adversarial training, where developers create attacks that try to elicit harmful behaviour, and says it remains imperfect: attackers keep devising new attacks that succeed, and safeguards are hard to evaluate under realistic conditions.
what_is_tested: Robustness of safeguards to adversarial attack (jailbreaks, prompt injection)
who_tests: Developers (adversarial training and attack generation), as described
interpretation_note: Describes limits of current practice; the body text does not use the term red teaming (it appears in cited titles only). Coded context.

framework: Advancing methods for agentic evaluations across domains: joint testing exercise, International Network of Advanced AI Measurement, Evaluation and Science (page published 17 July 2025, updated 1 June 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Describes a joint exercise by network members testing AI agents on leakage of sensitive information, fraud and cybersecurity, with the aim of improving testing methods rather than ranking models, and of checking how a system reached its result and not only the final answer.
what_is_tested: AI agents: sensitive information leakage, fraud, cybersecurity
who_tests: AI safety institutes and government mandated offices of several countries, with technical contributors
interpretation_note: A descriptive web page about a research exercise; no obligation and no protocol detail on the page itself. Coded context.

framework: Draft Framework Convention on artificial intelligence, human rights, democracy and the rule of law, CM(2024)52-prov1 (Ministers' Deputies, 15 March 2024)
requirement_paraphrase: Risk and impact management measures should, where appropriate, require testing of AI systems before they are first made available and when significantly modified.
what_is_tested: AI systems, impacts on human rights, democracy and the rule of law
who_tests: Not specified (to be set by each Party's measures)
interpretation_note: The text read is a draft marked prov1 and restricted pending Committee of Ministers examination, so nothing in it binds anyone. If adopted as drafted it would bind Parties (states), with the qualifier 'where appropriate' leaving discretion; wording and numbering may differ in the final convention. Fragment seen: 'testing of artificial intelligence systems before making them available for first use'. Modification wording is from the summary.

framework: Draft Framework Convention on artificial intelligence, human rights, democracy and the rule of law, CM(2024)52-prov1 (Ministers' Deputies, 15 March 2024)
requirement_paraphrase: Each Party is called on to enable, as appropriate, controlled environments for developing, experimenting with and testing AI systems under competent authority supervision. Article 3(3) excludes research and development of systems not yet made available, unless testing or similar activity may interfere with human rights, democracy or the rule of law.
what_is_tested: AI systems in controlled test environments
who_tests: Developers under supervision of competent authorities
interpretation_note: Draft text, not binding. Article 13 is hortatory ('is called upon'). Coded enabler. The Article 3(3) carve out means pre release testing falls inside scope only in the interference case, as summarised.

framework: MDCG 2019-11 Rev.1, Guidance on Qualification and Classification of Software in Regulation (EU) 2017/745 (MDR) and (EU) 2017/746 (IVDR), revised June 2025
requirement_paraphrase: Claims about a software's intended medical purpose must be supported by an appropriate level of clinical evidence under Article 7 of the MDR and IVDR; software that lacks this may not be CE marked or make those claims.
what_is_tested: Medical device software claims, clinical evidence
interpretation_note: MDCG guidance interprets binding regulations but is itself non binding; the underlying legal duty sits in the MDR and IVDR, which were not read. Not AI specific. Coded enabler because it concerns evidence behind claims rather than a test method.

framework: MDCG 2019-11 Rev.1, Guidance on Qualification and Classification of Software in Regulation (EU) 2017/745 (MDR) and (EU) 2017/746 (IVDR), revised June 2025
clause_or_page: Section 8 (Consideration of changes to an MDSW), p. 25
requirement_paraphrase: Safety and performance are to be ensured through a continuous process of clinical and/or performance evaluation and risk management, and the effect of changes to function, intended use, design and manufacturing on qualification and classification must be evaluated.
what_is_tested: Medical device software safety and performance over its lifecycle
interpretation_note: Guidance, non binding in itself. Section 1 (p. 4) includes Medical Device AI (MDAI) in scope and footnote 2 points to separate guidance on interplay with the AI Act; that guidance was not read.

framework: Good Machine Learning Practice for Medical Device Development: Guiding Principles (FDA, Health Canada, MHRA; October 2021)
clause_or_page: Principle 8, 'Testing Demonstrates Device Performance During Clinically Relevant Conditions'
requirement_paraphrase: Test plans should be statistically sound and produce clinically relevant performance data independent of the training data, taking into account the intended population, important subgroups and confounders.
what_is_tested: Machine learning enabled medical device performance under clinically relevant conditions
interpretation_note: Joint guiding principles from FDA, Health Canada and MHRA; non binding. Subgroup and confounder wording comes from the Health Canada copy; the FDA copy read through the summary gave the first part.

framework: Good Machine Learning Practice for Medical Device Development: Guiding Principles (FDA, Health Canada, MHRA; October 2021)
clause_or_page: Principle 4, 'Training Data Sets Are Independent of Test Sets'
requirement_paraphrase: Training and test datasets should be kept appropriately independent, considering and addressing dependence from patient, data acquisition and site factors.
what_is_tested: Test set independence from training data
interpretation_note: Non binding principle. The fetch summary first misnumbered this principle and then corrected it to Principle 4; the Health Canada copy independently lists it as Principle 04.

framework: Good Machine Learning Practice for Medical Device Development: Guiding Principles (Health Canada page, published 27 October 2021, last modified 29 July 2024)
requirement_paraphrase: Training and test datasets should be appropriately independent, with patient, data acquisition and site factors considered.
what_is_tested: Test set independence
interpretation_note: Same joint principles as the FDA copy; non binding. Health Canada is the publisher of this copy.

framework: Good Machine Learning Practice for Medical Device Development: Guiding Principles (Health Canada page, published 27 October 2021, last modified 29 July 2024)
requirement_paraphrase: Clinical benefits and risks should be used to set clinically meaningful performance goals for testing, with attention to global and local performance and input and output variability.
what_is_tested: Performance goals for testing
interpretation_note: Non binding. Sets how goals are chosen rather than a threshold value.

framework: Good Machine Learning Practice for Medical Device Development: Guiding Principles (Health Canada page, published 27 October 2021, last modified 29 July 2024)
clause_or_page: Principle 08, testing under clinically relevant conditions
requirement_paraphrase: Test plans should be statistically sound and generate clinically relevant performance data independent of the training set, covering the intended population, important subgroups and confounding factors.
what_is_tested: Device performance under clinically relevant conditions
interpretation_note: Non binding; mirrors the FDA copy.

framework: Roadmap for Artificial Intelligence Safety Assurance, Version I (FAA; issue date not stated in the text read)
clause_or_page: Section 'Assuring the Safety of AI', p. 20
requirement_paraphrase: States that validation of a learned AI system needs supplemental guidance, asking how to show a learned model performs as expected, and proposes treating the model as a mathematical function while treating its implementation as traditional engineering.
what_is_tested: Learned (design time fixed) AI model verification and validation
who_tests: Applicants and the FAA (certification framework to be developed)
interpretation_note: A roadmap, described in the text as a living point in time document that does not set the certification framework; many milestones are listed as ongoing, TBD or draft. Coded guidance.

framework: Roadmap for Artificial Intelligence Safety Assurance, Version I (FAA; issue date not stated in the text read)
clause_or_page: Section 'Application of Principles to Aircraft Certification', p. 16
requirement_paraphrase: Cites extensive stress testing of AI systems at item level to verify functionality, with further tests at system and aircraft level to address failure analysis.
what_is_tested: Learned AI at item, system and aircraft level
interpretation_note: Describes an approach rather than a requirement. Page 15 notes that existing DO-254 methods fall short for AI.

framework: Roadmap for Artificial Intelligence Safety Assurance, Version I (FAA; issue date not stated in the text read)
clause_or_page: Section 'Assuring the Safety of AI', pp. 20-21; 'Aviation Safety Research', p. 24
requirement_paraphrase: Explores Overarching Properties (intent, correctness, innocuity) as a basis for assurance case arguments matched to risk consequence, with FAA and NASA case studies reported as showing promise.
what_is_tested: Assurance case for AI enabled aircraft software
who_tests: Applicants, with FAA review, as envisaged
interpretation_note: A research direction, not a settled method; the text treats it as still under study.

framework: DoD Directive 3000.09, Autonomy in Weapon Systems (reissued 25 January 2023)
requirement_paraphrase: Autonomous and semi-autonomous weapon systems must pass rigorous hardware and software verification and validation and realistic developmental and operational test and evaluation; systems with AI capabilities get the same rigorous developmental and operational T&E. Systems must function as expected in realistic operational environments against adaptive adversaries.
what_is_tested: Weapon system hardware, software and AI capability behaviour in realistic operational conditions, including against adaptive adversaries
who_tests: DoD components (developers and test organisations; DOT&E oversees operational T&E standards and approves test plans, Sec. 2.5)
interpretation_note: Binding on the DoD organisations named in Sec. 1.1 as an internal directive, not on private parties. Excludes items listed in Sec. 1.1.b (for example unarmed platforms, autonomous cyberspace capabilities). Locators come from the tool's summary of the PDF.

framework: DoD Directive 3000.09, Autonomy in Weapon Systems (reissued 25 January 2023)
requirement_paraphrase: Before formal development a weapon system needs senior approval, and the review must verify that plans for V&V and T&E exist to establish reliability, effectiveness and related properties.
what_is_tested: Existence and adequacy of V&V and T&E plans at the pre-development gate
who_tests: USD(P), USD(R&E) and VCJCS approve; DoD component submits
interpretation_note: Binding on DoD senior reviewers and components. Quotation of the full list of properties was not seen; only the beginning of the plan requirement. Waiver route for urgent need at Sec. 4.2, p. 17.

framework: DoD Directive 3000.09, Autonomy in Weapon Systems (reissued 25 January 2023)
requirement_paraphrase: Before fielding, senior reviewers verify that system performance, capability, reliability, effectiveness and suitability have been assessed under realistic conditions; Sec. 4.1.d(3)(b) also asks for a demonstration that the system can be reprogrammed quickly enough.
what_is_tested: System performance, reliability, effectiveness and suitability under realistic conditions; reprogramming speed
who_tests: USD(P), USD(A&S) and VCJCS verify before fielding
interpretation_note: Pre-fielding gate with a test evidence requirement. Binding on DoD actors. Locator from summary, check against the PDF page.

framework: SR 11-7, Supervisory Guidance on Model Risk Management (dated 4 April 2011, last updated 19 August 2011 per page)
requirement_paraphrase: Validation covers evaluation of conceptual soundness (design, construction, documentation, empirical support), ongoing monitoring to confirm the model performs as intended, and outcomes analysis comparing model outputs with actual outcomes, including back-testing.
what_is_tested: Model design quality, in-use performance and agreement of outputs with realised outcomes
interpretation_note: Supervisory guidance, so non binding as a rule. The page text I saw did not say it was superseded (a separate listing note says SR 26-2 supersedes it; SR 26-2's own page supersedes it, see that row). Whether it applies to AI models is not stated in the passages seen. Pre-use validation was not stated as a distinct requirement in the summary.

framework: SR 11-7, Supervisory Guidance on Model Risk Management (dated 4 April 2011, last updated 19 August 2011 per page)
clause_or_page: Section 'Model Validation', independence passage (locator not seen)
requirement_paraphrase: Validation should involve a degree of independence from model development and use, generally performed by staff not responsible for development or use.
what_is_tested: Independence of the validation function
who_tests: Bank staff independent of development and use
interpretation_note: Enabler for credible testing. Wording paraphrased from the tool summary. OTHER used because independence is a governance condition and not a test type.

framework: SR 26-2, Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management (issued 17 April 2026)
clause_or_page: Section V (Model Validation and Monitoring), p. 9
requirement_paraphrase: Validation generally occurs before a model's first use; if urgent business need forces earlier use, the institution should attend to limitations and apply controls such as usage limits or closer monitoring.
what_is_tested: Model validation before first use
who_tests: Banking organisations (validation function independent of development)
interpretation_note: Interagency guidance issued by Federal Reserve, OCC and FDIC; guidance is non binding as a rule. Footnote 3, p. 4, puts generative AI and agentic AI outside scope, so it reaches traditional statistical and non generative AI models only. Page numbers are the attachment's own.

framework: SR 26-2, Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management (issued 17 April 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Model testing is a core part of development; it can include out-of-sample and out-of-time testing, comparison of alternative assumptions and assessment of data quality, with rigour matched to complexity and materiality.
what_is_tested: Model accuracy on held out data and time periods, data quality, sensitivity to assumptions
who_tests: Model developers at the banking organisation
interpretation_note: Non generative AI scope only (footnote 3, p. 4). Risk proportional testing language.

framework: CFPB Consumer Financial Protection Circular 2022-03 (published 26 May 2022)
requirement_paraphrase: Creditors may use post-hoc explanation methods but, because these approximate models, must still be able to validate the accuracy of the approximations, which may not be possible with less interpretable models.
what_is_tested: Accuracy of post-hoc explanations used for adverse action reasons
interpretation_note: Interpretive circular on adverse action notices; the page says nothing about withdrawal or rescission (only publication 26 May 2022 and last modified 28 August 2024). This is the only validation passage on the page and there is no separate testing requirement. Binding force of the circular itself was not assessed from the page, so coded as guidance.

framework: Principles for the Secure Integration of Artificial Intelligence in Operational Technology (CISA, ASD ACSC and partners, initial version 3 December 2025)
clause_or_page: Sec. 3.3, Conduct Thorough AI Testing and Evaluation, p. 17
requirement_paraphrase: Begin testing on infrastructure built for testing, start with low fidelity tests for fast iteration, move to more realistic non-production systems including hardware in the loop, and move into production for further testing only after sufficient non-production testing; keep production data out of test environments.
what_is_tested: AI behaviour in staged non-production environments (low fidelity, virtualised controllers, hardware in the loop)
who_tests: Operators and owners of OT systems integrating AI
interpretation_note: Joint guidance by CISA, ASD ACSC, NSA AISC, FBI, Canadian Cyber Centre, BSI, NCSC-NL, NCSC-NZ and NCSC-UK (authors per the tool summary). Non binding. Read on the ASD host.

framework: Principles for the Secure Integration of Artificial Intelligence in Operational Technology (CISA, ASD ACSC and partners, initial version 3 December 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: Regularly assess AI functions and test their resilience through offensive security exercises (red teaming), and continuously validate and refine AI models in simulated environments before deployment.
what_is_tested: AI resilience to attack; model behaviour in simulation
interpretation_note: Guidance only. The tool summary placed red teaming on p. 19 and simulation on p. 20; verify pages in the PDF.

framework: Principles for the Secure Integration of Artificial Intelligence in Operational Technology (CISA, ASD ACSC and partners, initial version 3 December 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: Treat AI systems like any new OT system and test them for safety impacts such as latency and interoperability, using test infrastructure before production deployment where possible, and provide failsafe reversion to traditional automation or manual control.
what_is_tested: Safety impact (latency, interoperability) and failsafe reversion
interpretation_note: Guidance only; failsafe item is an enabler for safe testing in production. Locators from summary.

framework: Texas H.B. 149, Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act (Senate Committee Report version, committee substitute)
requirement_paraphrase: A defendant may not be found liable where the violation was discovered through its own testing, including adversarial or red-team testing, or internal review, subject to the other conditions in the subsection.
what_is_tested: Adversarial and red-team testing as a route to a no-liability outcome
who_tests: Deployer or developer of the AI system (self testing)
interpretation_note: This is a Senate Committee Report version and committee substitute (reported 21 May 2025), not the enacted text, so it is not binding as read; enrolled text was not checked. The text does not use the words 'affirmative defense'. Sec. 552.105(e)(2)(D) separately references substantial compliance with the NIST AI RMF Generative AI Profile.

framework: Texas H.B. 149, Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act (Senate Committee Report version, committee substitute)
requirement_paraphrase: The department must create a regulatory sandbox where an approved person can test an AI system for a limited time and on a limited basis without a licence or other authorisation, for up to 36 months.
what_is_tested: Limited real-world testing of AI systems under regulator approval
who_tests: Sandbox participants, with department and agency approval
interpretation_note: Committee substitute text, not enacted as read. Sandbox is an enabler of testing, not a testing requirement.

framework: Ofcom, Red Teaming for GenAI Harms discussion paper (web page)
requirement_paraphrase: Ofcom describes red teaming as a type of AI model evaluation that attacks a model to see if it produces harmful content so safeguards can be added, and says there is no clear consensus on method, skills or outputs; the page says the paper sets out 10 practices but does not list them.
what_is_tested: Generative AI model vulnerability to harmful output generation
who_tests: AI developers and online services (by description)
interpretation_note: The page itself says the discussion paper does not constitute official guidance. The paper PDF was not opened; the 10 practices were not seen, so no clause level claims are made.

framework: MHRA, Software and AI as a Medical Device Change Programme roadmap (GOV.UK guidance; visible date 'Updated 14 June 2023')
clause_or_page: WP 9 AI RIG (AI Rigour), objective 3 and item WP9-04
requirement_paraphrase: The roadmap lists an objective to outline technical methods to test AI as a medical device so it is safe and effective, and plans best practice guidance on methods to assess AIaMD performance across the lifecycle.
what_is_tested: Performance and safety of AI as a medical device across the lifecycle; bias methods listed in WP9-05 to WP9-07
interpretation_note: Roadmap of planned deliverables, not itself binding; the page says much of the programme builds on legislation through guidance. Page does not confirm which drafts were published. Wording of WP9-04 and the objective read via summary.

framework: MHRA, Software and AI as a Medical Device Change Programme roadmap (GOV.UK guidance; visible date 'Updated 14 June 2023')
clause_or_page: WP 3 Premarket requirements, objective 1 and items WP3-01 and WP3-02
requirement_paraphrase: Planned work to ensure software as a medical device is supported by adequate data on safety, effectiveness and quality, including a review of essential requirements (secondary legislation) and best practice development and deployment guidance.
what_is_tested: Premarket evidence of safety, effectiveness and quality of software including AI
interpretation_note: Planned, not enacted; some items are described as secondary legislation, others as guidance. No testing method is specified here. Read via summary.

framework: Good machine learning practice for medical device development: guiding principles (MHRA, FDA, Health Canada; GOV.UK page showing 'Updated 5 October 2026', first published 27 October 2021)
clause_or_page: Guiding principle 4 (Training data sets are independent of test sets)
requirement_paraphrase: Training and test datasets should be selected and maintained to be appropriately independent, with all sources of dependence (such as patient, acquisition and site factors) addressed.
what_is_tested: Independence of test data from training data
interpretation_note: Joint non binding principles; the page states no formal legal status. Quoted phrase 'appropriately independent of one another' read via summary.

framework: Good machine learning practice for medical device development: guiding principles (MHRA, FDA, Health Canada; GOV.UK page showing 'Updated 5 October 2026', first published 27 October 2021)
clause_or_page: Guiding principle 8 (Testing demonstrates device performance during clinically relevant conditions)
requirement_paraphrase: Statistically sound test plans should be developed and executed to give clinically relevant performance information independently of the training data, considering patient populations, subgroups, clinical settings and confounders.
what_is_tested: Clinically relevant device performance including subgroups and confounding factors
interpretation_note: Non binding principle. Subgroup consideration also links to FAIR testing. Read via summary.

framework: Good machine learning practice for medical device development: guiding principles (MHRA, FDA, Health Canada; GOV.UK page showing 'Updated 5 October 2026', first published 27 October 2021)
clause_or_page: Guiding principle 6 (Model design is tailored to the available data and reflects the intended use of the device)
requirement_paraphrase: Model design should support mitigation of known risks such as overfitting, performance degradation and security risks, and clinical benefits and risks should inform the performance goals used for testing.
what_is_tested: Performance goals derived from clinical benefit and risk; mitigation of overfitting and degradation
interpretation_note: Non binding principle. The page heading and the sentence on performance goals were read via summary; the exact wording of goals may differ.

framework: Predetermined change control plans for machine learning enabled medical devices: guiding principles (MHRA, FDA, Health Canada; published 24 October 2023)
requirement_paraphrase: A predetermined change control plan should describe the specific planned changes and include methods for verifying and validating them, plus mechanisms to detect failures and revert or halt changes.
what_is_tested: Verification and validation of planned model changes
interpretation_note: Classed as guidance on the page, which does not state whether it is binding. Verification and validation wording is in supporting points read via summary.

framework: Predetermined change control plans for machine learning enabled medical devices: guiding principles (MHRA, FDA, Health Canada; published 24 October 2023)
requirement_paraphrase: The principle gives, as examples of transparency, comprehensive testing of planned changes and monitoring of, and response to, performance deviations.
what_is_tested: Testing of planned changes and monitoring of performance deviations
interpretation_note: Guidance. The testing reference is an example within the transparency principle, so it is a lighter provision than principle 1. Read via summary.

framework: FCA press release: FCA set to launch Live AI Testing service (first published 29/04/2025, last updated 05/12/2025)
clause_or_page: Press release body; no clause numbers
requirement_paraphrase: The FCA describes a service, proposed at the time of the release, where firms ready to deploy consumer or market facing AI models work with the FCA to check new AI tools are ready to be used.
what_is_tested: Readiness of consumer or market facing AI tools before deployment (criteria not specified)
interpretation_note: Press release describing a proposed 12 to 18 month service with planned launch September 2025; the page gives no test criteria. Whether the service later launched was not read here. Participation is described as support, not a requirement.

framework: NSW AI Assessment Framework (Digital NSW page, copyright 2026; no version number or update date seen)
clause_or_page: Section 'When to submit your project to the AI Review Committee'
requirement_paraphrase: AI systems whose self-assessment gives a high or critical risk must be submitted to the AI Secretariat for review by the AI Review Committee.
what_is_tested: Risk assessed through the AIAF self-assessment; committee review of high and critical risk systems
who_tests: NSW Government agencies (self-assessment), then AI Review Committee via AI Secretariat
interpretation_note: Binding on NSW Government agencies per the page's 'must' wording; the page does not set specific testing methods and the summary shows no explicit before deployment gate. Risk scale beyond high and critical not seen. The lister's note says a 2024 launch; the page read describes a later version.

framework: NSW AI Assessment Framework (Digital NSW page, copyright 2026; no version number or update date seen)
clause_or_page: Section 'When should it be used?' and 'Use the AIAF Platform', 'Complete an assessment where required'
requirement_paraphrase: Agencies must use the AIAF when designing, developing, deploying, procuring or using AI systems, register use cases on the AIAF Platform (mandatory from 30 September 2026) and complete an assessment where registration says one is required; assurance may include privacy, human rights or cyber security review.
what_is_tested: AI use cases across their lifecycle, assessed for risk with possible privacy, human rights and cyber security review
interpretation_note: Applies to NSW agencies. Page says assessment runs from planning through operation, so stage is lifecycle. No specific test or validation requirement was seen. Read via summary.

framework: APRA letter to industry on artificial intelligence (AI), dated April 2026 per page
clause_or_page: Observations for Executive Management, 'Traditional change management and assurance is in place but is not sufficient for dynamic AI solutions', expectations list, final bullet
requirement_paraphrase: APRA expects regulated entities to conduct comprehensive risk and information security assessments prior to deployment and throughout the lifecycle.
what_is_tested: Risk and information security of AI solutions before deployment and across the lifecycle
interpretation_note: Letter is not presented as binding; it sets out expectations on current observations. Binding duties come from existing prudential standards the letter says still apply. Read via summary.

framework: APRA letter to industry on artificial intelligence (AI), dated April 2026 per page
clause_or_page: Observations for Executive Management, 'AI threats are increasing, but information security practices are struggling to keep pace', expectations list, third bullet
requirement_paraphrase: APRA expects robust security testing across AI generated code, software components and libraries; it observed gaps in the scope and coverage of security testing programmes.
what_is_tested: Security of AI generated code, components and libraries
interpretation_note: Expectation in a non binding letter. Date and locator via summary; the page text does not specify test methods.

framework: AI Discussion Paper (AIディスカッションペーパー) version 1.0, Financial Services Agency, March 2025 (summary PDF)
requirement_paraphrase: Describes as a practice example that independent validators carry out verification of AI models before production use and continuous performance monitoring; also that institutions run proofs of concept on several vendors' tools to check model accuracy, and document model methodology including assumptions, limits and uncertainty.
what_is_tested: Model accuracy and validity before production use; ongoing performance
who_tests: Independent validators within the financial institution; institutions running PoCs
interpretation_note: Discussion paper that records observed industry practice; it sets no requirement. Section numbering shown as the summariser rendered it (circled numeral 2 read as 2). Only the summary PDF was read, not the main text.

framework: AI Discussion Paper (AIディスカッションペーパー) version 1.0, Financial Services Agency, March 2025 (summary PDF)
requirement_paraphrase: States that for generative AI there are no established systematic performance metrics, so development, operation and management structures are still being built.
what_is_tested: Performance evaluation of generative AI (metrics gap)
interpretation_note: Context only: records the absence of agreed evaluation metrics for generative AI, which limits what pre-deployment testing can measure.

framework: AI Discussion Paper (AIディスカッションペーパー) version 1.0, Financial Services Agency, March 2025 (summary PDF)
requirement_paraphrase: Says a consistent framework is needed to detect and address model bias early; notes that evaluation indicators and audit procedures are not yet clearly defined.
what_is_tested: Bias in AI models
interpretation_note: Wording of the need is hedged (a framework is 'required' in the descriptive sense); the paper is non binding. Locator is as given by the summariser.

framework: Guidelines on Ensuring Safety of Automated Driving Vehicles (自動運転車の安全確保に関するガイドライン), 2nd edition, revised 30 September 2025 (original 7 June 2024), MLIT
requirement_paraphrase: Safety of an automated driving vehicle is to be confirmed overall through simulation testing, test course driving tests and public road driving tests.
what_is_tested: Safety of automated driving vehicle (system level)
who_tests: Vehicle manufacturer or developer (actor not confirmed in the text read)
interpretation_note: Guideline document; status as binding or not not seen in the text read, so treated as guidance. Edition 2 revised 30 September 2025 per the fetched text.

framework: Guidelines on Ensuring Safety of Automated Driving Vehicles (自動運転車の安全確保に関するガイドライン), 2nd edition, revised 30 September 2025 (original 7 June 2024), MLIT
requirement_paraphrase: Scenario based safety evaluation: created scenarios and test cases are checked for conformity through simulation, test track driving and real traffic environment testing.
what_is_tested: Conformity of the vehicle with scenario test cases
who_tests: Vehicle manufacturer or developer (actor not confirmed in the text read)
interpretation_note: Scenario based evaluation combined across three test environments. Locator page numbers come from the summariser and may be approximate.

framework: Guidelines on Ensuring Safety of Automated Driving Vehicles (自動運転車の安全確保に関するガイドライン), 2nd edition, revised 30 September 2025 (original 7 June 2024), MLIT
requirement_paraphrase: Functional safety is to be ensured on the basis of ISO 26262 and ISO 21448 (SOTIF), and a safety evaluation framework based on ISO 35402 is to be applied.
what_is_tested: Functional safety and safety of the intended functionality
who_tests: Vehicle manufacturer or developer (actor not confirmed in the text read)
interpretation_note: The guideline names the standards without edition or date. The reading renders the third standard as ISO 35402 (no hyphen); the exact designation was not verified further.

framework: Review of Machine Learning-Enabled Medical Devices (機械学習を活用する医療機器の審査について), material 4, PMDA expert committee on AI-based software medical devices, undated
requirement_paraphrase: Validity of an ML medical device is judged on the evaluation data, not only on how the model was developed; evaluation data should reflect real clinical practice, though how much variation is needed is hard to determine.
what_is_tested: Validity and representativeness of evaluation data
who_tests: Regulatory reviewer (PMDA) assessing the applicant's evaluation
interpretation_note: Committee briefing material, not a binding rule. Undated; slide numbers are inferred from page footers by the summariser.

framework: Review of Machine Learning-Enabled Medical Devices (機械学習を活用する医療機器の審査について), material 4, PMDA expert committee on AI-based software medical devices, undated
requirement_paraphrase: Evaluation should cover the variations expected in clinical use (for example imaging conditions, patient population, lesion location, facility, realistic prevalence) to confirm there is no evident weakness; the slide says it is hard to explain objectively that coverage is comprehensive.
what_is_tested: Coverage of variation in evaluation data
interpretation_note: Slide raises open questions rather than fixing a standard.

framework: Review of Machine Learning-Enabled Medical Devices (機械学習を活用する医療機器の審査について), material 4, PMDA expert committee on AI-based software medical devices, undated
requirement_paraphrase: Warns that reusing evaluation data may lead to unnoticed optimisation to that data; suggests safeguards: check generalisation on a small separate dataset, cap the number of uses of the evaluation data, and set a model improvement process that assumes reuse.
what_is_tested: Generalisation and test data reuse
interpretation_note: These are suggested safeguards in committee material; not requirements.

framework: Review of Machine Learning-Enabled Medical Devices (機械学習を活用する医療機器の審査について), material 4, PMDA expert committee on AI-based software medical devices, undated
requirement_paraphrase: Use of the IDATEN change plan scheme is generally expected for adaptive devices; changes made under a confirmed change plan need no new approval if notified within the period set by ministerial ordinance; initial performance evaluation follows normal review.
what_is_tested: Change management of ML device after approval
interpretation_note: The slide quotes legal wording for the scheme, but the document itself is briefing material. The legal status of the scheme was not checked in the primary statute.

framework: Regulatory Guidelines for Software Medical Devices: A Life Cycle Approach, GL-04-R2, Revision 2.0, April 2022, HSA
requirement_paraphrase: The registration file for an AI medical device should include a test protocol and test report covering verification and validation against the performance specification, including acceptance limits and anomalies; performance claims such as sensitivity and specificity must be backed by these reports.
what_is_tested: Verification and validation of the AI medical device against its performance specification
interpretation_note: HSA guidance on registration content; wording 'should be provided' read via summary. The lister notes a later revision (GL-04-R4, 2025) exists; this row reflects Revision 2.0 only.

framework: Regulatory Guidelines for Software Medical Devices: A Life Cycle Approach, GL-04-R2, Revision 2.0, April 2022, HSA
clause_or_page: Section 9.1, AI model selection and dataset, p. 34
requirement_paraphrase: Model evaluation should be done with a test dataset that is separate from the training dataset; the developer should also ensure there is no duplication between training and validation datasets.
what_is_tested: Held out test data for model evaluation
interpretation_note: Quoted passage is from the summary of the page; locator is page 34 per the summariser.

framework: Regulatory Guidelines for Software Medical Devices: A Life Cycle Approach, GL-04-R2, Revision 2.0, April 2022, HSA
requirement_paraphrase: Presence of a valid clinical association between the AI medical device's output and its targeted clinical condition should be presented; clinical evaluation measures include sensitivity, specificity and predictive values.
what_is_tested: Clinical association and clinical validation of output
interpretation_note: Locators combine two sections as reported by the summariser.

framework: Consumer Protection in respect of Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence, HKMA circular dated 19 August 2024 (as stated in the fetched text)
requirement_paraphrase: Authorised institutions should ensure proper validation of generative AI models is in place and, early in deploying customer facing applications, keep a human in the loop over decisions.
what_is_tested: Validation of generative AI models for customer facing use
interpretation_note: The circular has no numbered paragraphs, so sub section letters and pages are the locators. Circular is supervisory guidance; its legal force was not read. The lister noted that Annex 1 body text did not show; this row uses only the circular itself.

framework: Consumer Protection in respect of Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence, HKMA circular dated 19 August 2024 (as stated in the fetched text)
requirement_paraphrase: Institutions should consider preventing unfair bias, including by adjusting to remove bias during the validation and review process, anonymising some data categories and using representative datasets.
what_is_tested: Bias in generative AI outputs
interpretation_note: Listed as one of several measures to consider; not an obligation.

framework: Guidelines for Financial Institutions Adopting Enabling Technologies, issued 15/11/2021, status shown as In-Force on the CBUAE Rulebook page
requirement_paraphrase: Institutions must ensure proper validation of Big Data Analytics and AI applications prior to their launch, with ongoing training, calibration and review afterwards.
what_is_tested: Validation of AI applications before launch
who_tests: The financial institution (internal or external validator)
interpretation_note: Wording says 'ensure' within a document titled Guidelines, so whether it binds as an enforceable rule was not settled from the text read. The page shows an In-Force status line. Clause 2.28 in Section 2 covers a similar review duty.

framework: Guidelines for Financial Institutions Adopting Enabling Technologies, issued 15/11/2021, status shown as In-Force on the CBUAE Rulebook page
requirement_paraphrase: Where relevant, institutions should carry out rigorous, independent validation and testing of material trained models before deployment, by an internal independent function or an external organisation; models should be checked for unintuitive or false causal relationships.
what_is_tested: Material trained Big Data Analytics and AI models
who_tests: Internal independent function or external organisation
interpretation_note: 'Should' wording in guidelines read as non binding recommendation; scope limited to material models.

framework: Guidelines for Financial Institutions Adopting Enabling Technologies, issued 15/11/2021, status shown as In-Force on the CBUAE Rulebook page
requirement_paraphrase: Institutions should establish an approved, documented framework to review the reliability, fairness, accuracy and relevance of algorithms, models and data, applied before deployment of a material application and periodically after.
what_is_tested: Reliability, fairness, accuracy and relevance of algorithms, models and data
interpretation_note: Clause 2.28 in Section 2 has parallel wording; the page text read was split across two fetches so 3.x clauses were taken from the second half.

framework: Guidelines for Financial Institutions Adopting Enabling Technologies, issued 15/11/2021, status shown as In-Force on the CBUAE Rulebook page
requirement_paraphrase: Institutions should keep design documentation for material models, including the form and frequency of validation, monitoring and review.
what_is_tested: Documentation of model validation arrangements
interpretation_note: Enabler for audit of validation; read through summary.
